sources.name: Blender Open Data benchmark snapshots

sources.name: FRED, Federal Reserve Economic Data
sources.licence: FRED API Terms of Use (https://fred.stlouisfed.org/docs/api/terms_of_use.html). The terms require the notice "This product uses the FRED® API but is not endorsed or certified by the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis", which the site prints. Series owned by third parties carry the word "Copyright" in their notes and need the owner's permission beyond personal use, so the catalogue holds only series published by US federal agencies (public domain) and the collector stops on any series whose notes say Copyright. The terms do not address storing data.
sources.frequency: weekly collection; most series are monthly
sources.typical_lag: two to eight weeks after the month ends, depending on the series

limitations: Every power figure is rated, not measured: CPU TDP (Intel's processor base power) and GPU reference board power, entered by hand from manufacturers' specifications (pdi/tech_value/cpu_specs.py, pdi/tech_value/gpu_specs.py). Real draw under a Blender render can be 30% or more away from the label, and Intel desktop chips boost well above their base power.
Performance is the Blender Open Data median score (samples per minute) in one Blender version. CPU and GPU scores use different backends and are never compared with each other.
Laptop chips and Apple silicon are left out: their power limit is set by the laptop maker or not published.
The cost calculator charges electricity only for the hours under load, because no idle power figure exists yet. The default rate is the BLS US city average price per kWh.
